notes.body:
Physiologically based pharmacokinetic/ pharmacodynamic (PBPK/PD) model rivaroxaban (body model)
Rivaroxaban, a direct oral anticoagulant (DOAC), is a widely used drug for the prevention and treatment of thromboembolic disorders. While its fixed dosing regimen and predictable anticoagulation profile improve clinical usability, significant inter-individual variability in pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD) exists, particularly in patients with altered physiology or comorbidities. This study established an open database of rivaroxaban PK and PD data from 14 clinical studies. The data were used to develop and validate a physiologically based pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PBPK/PD) model of rivaroxaban that captures its absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and coagulation effects. The model incorporates the effects of dose, food intake, hepatic and renal function, and allows simulation of activated Factor X (Factor Xa) inhibition, prothrombin time (PT), and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT). Simulations accurately reproduced observed plasma concentration-time and coagulation profiles across a range of doses, fed/fasting conditions, as well as with different degrees of cirrhosis and renal impairment. This mechanistic PBPK/PD model provides a framework for exploring variability in rivaroxaban response across diverse clinical scenarios and supports its use in personalized dosing strategies, clinical trial design, and regulatory evaluation.

parameter.name: relative increase of the PT per rivaroxaban concentration

body.p: The PT is linear in the total concentration of rivaroxaban in plasma; the PT of 10 mg in the fasted state rises to about 1.44 times its baseline at a Cmax of about 0.26 µM (Neoplastin Plus, Kubitza2006), the less sensitive reagents of the other studies give smaller increases.
The value of PT_slope is the result of the fit PD_20261018_082509__94e87, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

blockquote.p: 1.0: increased kidney function 1.0: normal kidney function (healthy control) <1.0: decreased kidney function

body.p: Renal function relative to the healthy glomerular filtration rate GFR_base, which is 101 ml/min at 75 kg; a measured creatinine clearance of X ml/min is the renal function X/101.
7.9 % unbound in the plasma of healthy subjects (Kubitza2013), 92-95 % bound to plasma proteins, mainly albumin.

parameter.name: renal clearance of unbound rivaroxaban relative to the GFR

body.p: The renal clearance of rivaroxaban is RIVEX_f times the filtration of its unbound fraction, fu_riv * GFR: 1 is filtration alone, above 1 a net secretion. Rivaroxaban is secreted by P-gp and BCRP, about two thirds of the renal clearance of 2.4-3.1 l/hr are active (Mueck2014, Kubitza2013); 36-42 % of a small oral dose are excreted unchanged in the urine (Weinz2009, Kubitza2005a), i.e. RIVEX_f about 6-8.
The value of KI__RIVEX_f is the result of the fit PK_20261018_075718__82026, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

Activity of the renal efflux transporters (P-gp, BCRP) relative to normal: 1.0 normal, <1.0 inhibition, >1.0 induction. It scales the secretion, (RIVEX_f - 1), not the filtration; set by the experiments of the coadministrations with documented factors, not fitted.

parameter.name: renal clearance of the rivaroxaban metabolites relative to the GFR

body.p: The renal clearance of the metabolites is RXEX_f times the GFR; the metabolites are about 11 % of the radioactivity in plasma after [14C]rivaroxaban (Weinz2009), so they are cleared faster than they are filtered.

parameter.name: rate for rivaroxaban metabolite export in bile

body.p: Biliary excretion of the metabolites: of an oral solution of 10 mg [14C]rivaroxaban 65.7 % of the dose are recovered in the urine (36 % unchanged) and 28.0 % in the feces (7 % unchanged), i.e. about 30 % of the dose are metabolites in the urine and 21 % in the feces (Weinz2009).
The value of LI__RXEX_BI_k is the result of the fit PK_20261018_075718__82026, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: fraction of the hepatic metabolism by CYP3A4

body.p: Rivaroxaban is metabolized by CYP3A4 (about 18 % of the dose), CYP2J2 (about 14 %) and CYP independent hydrolysis (about 14 %) (Mueck2014), so CYP3A4 is about 18/46 = 0.4 of the hepatic metabolism.
Intrinsic hepatic clearance per liver volume; the total clearance of rivaroxaban is about 10 l/hr, of which about 6-7 l/hr are non-renal (Mueck2014).
The value of LI__RIV2RX_k is the result of the fit PK_20261018_075718__82026, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: fraction absorbed of the dissolved rivaroxaban

body.p: Fraction of the dissolved rivaroxaban in the lumen of the intestine which is absorbed, the rest (1 - F_riv_abs) is excreted with the feces. 7 % of an oral solution of 10 mg [14C]rivaroxaban is excreted unchanged with the feces (Weinz2009), so 0.93. The dose dependent and the food dependent bioavailability of the tablets are the dissolution, see Vmax_dis_riv and fed.
First order absorption of the dissolved rivaroxaban, including the passage of an oral solution from the stomach: the tmax of an oral solution is about 0.5 hr (Kubitza2005a, Weinz2009).
The value of GU__RIVABS_k is the result of the fit PK_20261018_075718__82026, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

The dose is taken in the fasted state (0) or with a meal (1). The effects of food on the solubility and on the gastric emptying are FED_f_solubility and FED_f_emptying.

Factor of the capacity of the dissolution Vmax_dis_riv with food (bile micelles): food increases the AUC of 20 mg by 39 % and of 10 mg by 28 % (Kubitza2006), the bioavailability of 20 mg is about 66 % fasted and about 100 % fed.
The value of GU__FED_f_solubility is the result of the fit PK_20261018_075718__82026, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: rate of a stage of the gastric emptying of the tablet

body.p: The gastric emptying of a tablet in the fasted state passes N_EMPTYING = 3 stages with this rate (fitted), the mean residence time in the stomach is 3 stages divided by the rate.
The value of GU__Ka_emptying_riv is the result of the fit PK_20261018_075718__82026, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

The maximal rate of the dissolution of undissolved rivaroxaban in the intestine in the fasted state (solubility). The Cmax of the tablets rises less than the dose above 10 mg, 141, 173, 234 and 316 µg/l at 10, 20, 40 and 80 mg (Kubitza2005a), the tmax of 10 mg is 2.75 hr (Kubitza2006).
The value of GU__Vmax_dis_riv is the result of the fit PK_20261018_075718__82026, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: undissolved amount of half-maximal dissolution rivaroxaban

body.p: The dissolution saturates at a small undissolved amount: a dose of a tablet dissolves with the capacity Vmax_dis_riv, the remainder below Km_dis_riv with the first order rate Vmax_dis_riv/Km_dis_riv.

parameter.name: rate of the transit of undissolved rivaroxaban

body.p: The undissolved rivaroxaban leaves the absorptive part of the intestine and is excreted with the feces, the small intestinal transit of about 3-4 hr; it limits the fraction of a high dose which dissolves.
The value of GU__ktransit_riv is the result of the fit PK_20261018_075718__82026, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

Transit of the metabolites which are excreted with the bile into the feces, a mean transit time of about 36 hr: the fecal radioactivity of [14C]rivaroxaban is recovered within 2-4 days (Weinz2009). The rate does not change the amount which is excreted.
log(2) ~ 0.693 used for conversion of half-life injection time to injection rate.

Oxidative degradation of the morpholinone moiety by CYP3A4 and CYP2J2 and CYP independent hydrolysis of the amide bonds into a variety of metabolites, which are lumped (Weinz2009); the part of CYP3A4 is changed by f_cyp3a4.
